segments.summary: Reviewed SP-086 through SP-092 exactly and adversarially; payload, account invalidation, authored copy, freshness, retention, and provider/runtime family contracts expose schema, atomicity, localization, lifecycle, and ownership gaps.

Reviewed SP-093 through SP-099 exactly and adversarially; decomposed session families and debug/bundle migration boundaries are explicit, while restore concurrency, privacy, readiness, binding lifecycle, and interrupted migration remain underspecified.

Reviewed SP-100 through SP-105 exactly and adversarially; field minima, GHA state, annotation lineage, registry approvals, reanchoring, and revision runs need stronger invariants, concurrency, idempotency, and recovery oracles.

Reviewed SP-106 through SP-111 exactly and adversarially; composer/capture, audit events, browser persistence, artifact checkpoints, and worktree/lane projections have material privacy, concurrency, checkpoint, and deletion-propagation gaps.

Reviewed SP-112 through SP-117 exactly and adversarially; event sets and identity minima are broad, but ordering, optional-field invariants, join lifecycle, traceability, resolver precedence, and state-transition oracles remain incomplete.

Reviewed SP-118 through SP-123 exactly and adversarially; canonical ownership is generally strong, while missing-identity recovery, derived projection publication, route trust, alias migration, and terminal layout invalid-state rules need closure.

Reviewed SP-124 through SP-129 exactly and adversarially; restore identity and no-fake-liveness rules are strong, while partial restore, dangling refs, settings precedence, migration crash recovery, and stale-lock handling remain open.

Reviewed SP-130 through SP-135 exactly and adversarially; ledger boundaries and atomic rewrite intent are strong, but snapshot bounds, directory durability, root validation, backup integrity, lock lifecycle, and numeric retention limits remain high-risk gaps.
